claims.text: The terbium-free refractory high-entropy alloy exhibits superconductivity.
Terbium can be incorporated into the high-entropy alloy through arc melting.
Terbium atoms form localized magnetic sites within the alloy matrix.
The localized sites introduced by terbium possess magnetic moments.
Terbium-derived magnetic moments produce magnetic scattering.
Magnetic scattering from terbium disrupts Cooper-pair formation through pair breaking.
Terbium-induced magnetic pair breaking weakens the effective electron–phonon superconducting mechanism.
Electron–phonon coupling is responsible for superconductivity in the proposed refractory high-entropy alloy.
Terbium alloying will lower the superconducting transition temperature relative to a terbium-free baseline.
Terbium alloying may alter the critical magnetic fields relative to the terbium-free baseline.
The terbium-free baseline has a higher transition temperature and unperturbed superconducting properties.
The proposed effect requires enough terbium to introduce dispersed magnetic impurities without causing phase separation or major compositional changes.
Extremely low terbium concentrations may cause only minimal changes in superconducting behavior.
Excessively high terbium concentrations may cause structural instability or other emergent phenomena.
The magnitude and concentration dependence of the transition-temperature reduction depend on terbium distribution and alloy microstructure.
A controlled comparison should use terbium-containing and terbium-free samples with identical processing parameters and thermal histories.
Failure to observe a statistically significant transition-temperature decrease in the terbium-alloyed samples would falsify the proposed terbium-induced pair-breaking hypothesis.
